IS : 11256( Part 1) - 1985

Indian Standard
METHOD OF TEST FOR DETERMINATION OF THERMAL ENDURANCE OF INSULATING VARNISHES
PART 1 ELECTRIC STRENGTH METHOD

O.FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 1 ) was adopted by the lndian Standards Institution on 5 February 1985, after the draft finalized by the Solid Electrical Insulating Materials Sectional Committee had been approved. by the Eiectrotechnical Division Council.
0.2 A major

factor affecting the life of a cured film of an insulating varnish is thermal.degradation. Other factors, such .as moisture and vibration themselves normally do not cause failures, but arekconditiorrs that result in failure only after the cured varnish film has been weekened by thermal degradation. 0.3 A cured film of an insu!ating varnish is effective in protecting electrical equipment only as long as it retains its physical and electrical integrity. Generally as a result of thermal degradation, a cured film of sn insulating varnish undergoes changes, such as: a) loss of mass, b) reduction in flexibility, and c) porosity and crazing. 0.4 Of the various methods which can detect the effect of thermal degradation of cured films of insulating varnishes, the following methods are considered for determining thermal endurance of insulating varnishes after ageing at elevated temperatures: a) Reduction of electric strength, b) Loss of mass, and c) Bond strength by helical coil method. 0.5 This standard laj+ down three- diffeient methods -for-deterinfning the thermal endurance of insulating varnishes, which are-c%vered in'. __ _. _ _._. ._.. -. ..---.three parts as follows: Part 1 Electrical strength method, 3

IS : 11256 ( Part 1) - 1985

Part 2 Measurement of loss of mass, and Part 3 Bond strength by helical coil method. 0.6 This standard ( Part relative thermal endurance electric strength.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part 1 ) covers a test method for determining ahe thermal endurance of electrical insulating varnishes by means of coating on glass cloth and measuring electric strength before , and I.after heat . ~ ageing. &TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, ( Part I)-1981* shall apply. 3. .TEST SPECIMEN 3.0 Test specimens shall consist of panels of continuous glass Lath coated with varnish by dipping. ,.

the definitions given in IS :' .10026

filament, woven

3.1 Preparation of Glass Cloth Panels - The glass cloth panels shall be cut from continuous filament woven glass 0'1 to 0'18 mm thick with a weight per unit area of 90 g/m2 to 140 g/m2 and with 20 to 26 ends and 16 to 24 picks per centimetre. The glass cloth shall be heat cleaned to remove binders. The desized cloth should not contain residual size more than 0'2 percent. NOTE - A suggested heat cleaning procedure consists of heating the cloth 24
hours at 250�C and 24 hours at 400�C.

CAUTION-Heating above 45O'C may damage the cloth. Each panel of glass cloth shall be 15 x 30 cm with the 30 cm dimension parallel to the warp threads of the cloth. Each panel shall be mounted and fastened in a suitable specimenholding frame. *Specification for insulating varnishes containing solvents: Part I .Definitions and general requirements.
4

NOTE - Such a frame is made by using a I m length of corrosion-resistant wire ( for exnmple, tinned M.S. ) approximately 1.7 mm in diameter bent to form a rectangle, having inside dimensions of 15 x 30 cm. The ends of the wire mzy overlap about 5 cm at one corner and be fastened together.

A set of ten to twelve panels is required for each ageing temperatrue. A suitable fixture shall be used for holding the specimen frames in the oven in a vertical position with a minimum spacing of 2'5 cm. 3.2 Varnish Dipping and Drying/Curing of Glass Cloth Panels - Test specimens shall be prepared by dipping the mounted glass cloth panels in the varnish at the ambient temperature. The consistency of the varnish shall be adjusted by. trial so that two or more coats will give an increase in thickness of The panel shall be immersed 0'083 0'005 mm over the cloth thickness. in the varnish in the direction. of the 30 cm length until bubbling stops. It shall be mechanically withdrawn at a uniform rate of 10 cm/min and _ allowed to drain for 30 minutes. Glass cloth panels shall be reversed endwise between subsequent dips to provide a more uniform coat. Af'ter each dip, the specimens shall be dried/baked in the same vertical position last dip and at the temperature and ,the time specified by the varnish manufacturer:
: 4. TEST APPARATUS 4.1' The electrodes _: ..* 8,

shall consist of opposing brass rods 75 mm ( bottom ) and 38 mm ( top ) with edges rounded to a radius of I'0 mm. The electrode faces shall be smooth, flat and the electrodes shall be held exactly opposite one another. The upper electrode shall be movable. Any suitable holding and guiding arrangement, meeting the requirements will serve the purpose. 4.2 Electric Strength Test Set - The equipment for testing electric strength shall be as described in IS : 2584-1963*. 4.3 Ageing Ovens - The air circulating ovens shall be such that the tsinperatures inside the oven do not vary by more than h2'C from the specified temperature. 5. IS : 11256 ( Part 1) - 1985 To reduce the error in extra-polating thermal endurance data and to obtain the temperature index, the lowest ageing temperature should be chosen so that an extra-po!ation exceeding 20�C should not be necessary. Choose the exposure temperature so that any essentially linear portion of the life data curve ( log of time to failure v/s the reciprocal of the absolute temperature ) is well established. For suitable exposure temperature ranges refer Tab!e I of IS : 8504 ( Part 1 )-1977*. 6: TESTING PROCEDURE 6.1 Specimen Thickness - The average initial thickness of each specimen shall be measured at five points before heat ageing. The .thickness shall be determined along the centre of the specimen parallel to its 30 cm length. 6.2 Ihi?i~l I?&ctr& $trengttb `Vo!tage 7. C&e Ispe&nen from each set of specimens &all be .conditioned for at least ,4,hours at 27 * 2�C and at standard atmospheric conditions ( see IS : 2260- I973t ) and then tested for electric strength by the short-time test according to IS: 2584-1963s except that a rate of rise of 500 V/set shall be used. Six electric strength measurements shall be made- 45. cm from one end of the specimen. Tn alternate I, the specimen shall. be inserted in the curved electrode fixture so that the warp threads are bent. In each alternative, the electrode is lowered slowly taking care to avoid injury to the specimen. 63 Ageing snd Specimen Testing - Five specimens shall be tagged with aluminium foil or otherwise permanently identified and placed in the specimen holding frames as described in 3.1. The fixture containing the specimen frames shall then be placed in the ageing oven and positioned so that it is at least 10 cm from the walls at any point and thus the specimens are held parallel to the direction of the air flow. One specimen sha!l be removed at the end of each of three ageing times equal to 25 percent, 50 percent and IO0 percent of the estimated thermal life at the selected ageing temperature. After removal, the specimens

shall be conditioned for at least 4 hours at 27 f 2�C at standard atmospheric conditions and then subjected to the electric strength test according to alternative I or alternative 2. At the time of 50 percent of estimated thermal life, five additional specimens shall be tagged and placed in the oven. Similarly, at the time of 75 percent of thermal life, the remaining specimens shall be placed in the oven. Plot on suitable graph paper the average electric strength of each specimen as the ordinate, corresponding to the ageing time as the abscissa.. If the thermal life has been under estimated, one specimen of the first group remaining in the oven shall be removed at 150 percent of the estimated thermal life and tested. With information now avai.able on aged specimens, each of the remaining specimens shall be removed at chosen intervals so as to establish a curve of electric strength versus exposure time. This may require filling in between established points or extending beyond if necessary. This procedure assures that sufficient specimens are available to complete the ageing process. The ageing shall be continued until a breakdown voltage of b of the specified end-point voltage is reached or until the ageing time has progressed not less than 6 000 h. If a thermal life of more than 5 000 h is estimated at certain ageing temperatures, the upper limit shall be extended accordingly. 7. ELECTRIC STRENGTH END POINT

7.1 An end point of 12 kv/mm is recommended as the failure criteria. The selection of this end point is arbitrary and based upon experience showing that value corelates with actual service life. 7.2 When agreed upon, other end points, such as a percentage of the initial average unaged electric strength may be also used. 8. 8.3 Determination of temperature index or thermal endurance per 11.4 of IS : 8504 ( Part 1 )-1977*.
